context: The .oma state directory has four incompatible resolution contracts. Hooks read/write <project>/.oma via src/utils.ts resolveOmaDir (AUGMENT_PROJECT_DIR|WORKSPACE_ROOT|cwd); the MCP server (plugins/oma/mcp/state-server.mjs) derives OMA_DIR as join(__dirname,'..','.oma') - the plugin install dir - and ignores the OMA_DIR env var that e2e/oma-cli.bats passes it; src/utils.ts findOmaDir uses OMA_DIR env + cwd walk-up + ~/.oma; vscode-oma reads <workspaceRoot>/.oma. State forks per entry point: when installed from a marketplace cache, oma_mode_set persists shared state into the install dir, writeState throws JSON-RPC -32603 on read-only install dirs, and oma_skill_list/oma_skill_inject are cwd-relative and fail when cwd is not the repo root. SPEC.md/ADR-0001 state each working copy gets its own MCP server for state persistence.
root_causes: state-server.mjs is outside the TS build and re-derives dir logic by hand instead of consuming the shared contract
no test ever pinned where state-server.mjs writes state; the bats suite passed vacuously because a missing team dir yields {ok:true,workers:[]}
evidence: plugins/oma/mcp/state-server.mjs:15 OMA_DIR = join(__dirname, '..', '.oma') ignores the OMA_DIR env var
e2e/oma-cli.bats passes OMA_DIR to the MCP server and the test still passes with the var ignored (vacuous)

docs/specifications/ACTIVE/consolidate-oma-utils.md declares unifying the resolvers a non-goal 'requires its own ADR'; its scope covers CLI-vs-hook discovery, not the MCP server's __dirname derivation, which no doc claims
solutions: one canonical resolveOmaDir contract (OMA_DIR env -> AUGMENT_PROJECT_DIR -> cwd walk-up -> ~/.oma) in a single dependency-free module consumed by state-server.mjs; align src/utils.ts to the same precedence order
state-server.mjs consumes the shared module (relative .mjs import, zero npm deps preserved) instead of re-deriving OMA_DIR via __dirname
skills paths in state-server.mjs resolve relative to the plugin install root (__dirname) instead of cwd, since skills ship with the plugin
vscode-oma consumes the same contract via its state adapter if its build supports the cross-package import; otherwise pin its resolution to the same precedence order with a parity test

add a real test surface: spawn the actual state-server.mjs process with OMA_DIR set, speak JSON-RPC, assert state lands in the OMA_DIR dir; add a parity test asserting the shared module and src/utils.ts agree on a scenario matrix
acceptance_criteria: state-server.mjs honors the OMA_DIR env var; state written via oma_mode_set lands under $OMA_DIR (spawn test proves it)
state-server.mjs never persists state into the plugin install dir via __dirname derivation
one shared module is the only place the dir-resolution contract is implemented for the MCP server; src/utils.ts and the shared module agree on a documented precedence matrix (parity test)
skills paths resolve from the plugin install root, working from any cwd
npm test passes with the new spawn + parity tests included in the suite
no npm dependencies added; state-server.mjs stays zero-dep plain .mjs
